panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (i, ii, iii). i: Panel i shows palms of woman in chronic arsenic poisoning household investigation; in-text explicitly states pigmentation, de-pigmentation and hyperkeratosis on palms and soles. ii: Panel ii shows soles of same woman; same in-text description of pigmentation, de-pigmentation and hyperkeratosis on palms and soles applies. iii: Panel iii shows scaly erythematous plaque on right arm with ruler; in disease-focused chronic arsenic poisoning article this corresponds to arsenical Bowen disease plaque, classic cutaneous malignancy in arsenicosis.

in_text_mentions: As shown in Figure 1, significant pigmentation, de-pigmentation and hyperkeratosis were found on her palms and soles. A 3-cm scaly, erythematous plaque was also detected on her right arm. The woman told us that her family members had similar skin features, some of which were more serious. We then immediately went to the woman’s family to initiate an investigation.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A shows bilateral palms with yellowish hyperkeratotic papules/plaques in 51-year-old man with 9-year realgar use; caption and article title attribute to arsenical keratosis of chronic arsenic poisoning. B: Panel B shows bilateral soles with diffuse verrucous yellowish hyperkeratotic papules/plaques in same patient with realgar-induced chronic arsenic poisoning; caption explicitly describes arsenical keratosis.

in_text_mentions: A 51‐year‐old man presented with a 7‐year history of asymptomatic keratinizing skin lesions (Figure 1A, B). On physical examination, diffuse verrucous, yellowish, hyperkeratotic papules, and plaques were observed on bilateral palms, soles, and fingers. findings.label: Palmoplantar arsenical keratoses
findings.evidence: Partial view of hyperkeratosis and verrucous hyperplasia of the palm with a diameter of 0.2–0.4 cm.

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of the left palm showing multiple discrete hyperkeratotic papules and verrucous hyperplasia, explicitly diagnosed as arsenical keratosis in a patient with chronic arsenic poisoning from long-term realgar ingestion. The caption and in-text mentions directly attribute the lesion to chronic arsenic poisoning, making this a textbook presentation of palmoplantar arsenical keratosis.
panels.attribution_text: Liu et al. Psoriasis complicated with arsenical keratosis and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: a case report.. Frontiers in oncology 2024. doi:10.3389/fonc.2024.1415444. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Left hand. Partial view of hyperkeratosis and verrucous hyperplasia of the palm with a diameter of 0.2–0.4 cm.
in_text_mentions: Chinese and Western Medicine Oncology of our hospital with a history of nearly 30 years of psoriasis on 25 June 2023 due to “abscess, ulceration, and pain after trauma of the right thumb for one and a half years.” The patient was treated in Peking University First Hospital, and the skin lesions of the palm were diagnosed as arsenical keratosis ( Figure 1 ). The patient was considered to have chronic arsenic poisoning caused by previous treatment of psoriasis without the guidance of physicians. He reported oral administration of realgar (with As4S4 as the major component) for at least 25 years.
